At 0% progress, prioritize **jointly learned title/description fusion within the corrected GRU4Rec**, subject to bounded implementation checks. This remains untested; the inspiration’s 0.5687 score is historical evidence, not this proposal’s result.

Three starting insights guide the experiment. Scalar retention addresses stale interests but does not enrich item identity. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled ranking-error rate and 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin motivate discrimination improvements. Mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 provide no evidence supporting a collapse penalty.

Three literature insights qualify the direction. Feature-rich recurrent recommendation already combines lexical features and IDs [6], reducing originality. CLA-Rec and ITS-Rec motivate text alignment but use prohibited pretrained encoders or unavailable inputs [1,2]; TedRec cautions that direct fusion can be ineffective [7]. GRU4Rec supports BPR-max [3], while Hard-BPR warns about false negatives [4].

The framework separates **representation**, **objective**, and **memory** interventions. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each assessment includes supporting (+) and limiting (−) reasons.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ID–text fusion [1,2,6,7] | 2: +constrained adaptation; −close precedent | 7: +cross-item sharing; −text noise | 7: +specific connections; −no compatibility guarantee | 7: +discrimination hypothesis; −unmeasured ranks | 6: +small encoder; −interfaces/caching |
| Uniform-pool BPR-max [3,4] | 2: +targeted application; −established loss | 6: +ranking signal; −sampling sensitivity | 4: +ordering; −no richer identity | 8: +confusing negatives; −false negatives | 3: +localized change; −pooling cost |
| Fast/slow GRU state [5] | 4: +task adaptation; −temporal precedent | 7: +changing interests; −identifiability | 7: +recent/old distinction; −limited semantics | 6: +context; −indirect evidence | 7: +single network; −recurrence changes |

Fusion remains selected because it targets two user failures: products lacking a specific purpose connection and media lacking identifiable artist/story/style connections. It also targets Electronics’ weak separation. These are hypotheses; text cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, or current mood.

Use randomly initialized token embeddings, masked mean pooling, and a projected text residual gated against ID embeddings. Share the representation between GRU inputs and candidate scoring; initially preserve loss, sampler, optimizer, and schedule.

```python
text = masked_sum(token_embedding(tokens)) / count.clamp_min(1)
gate = sigmoid(gate_layer(concat(id_vector, text)))
item = id_vector + gate * project(text) * has_text
features = corrected_gru(item_history)
score = dot(final_nonpadding_feature(features), candidate_item)
```

Initialize the gate near 0.1; zero missing-text and padding contributions. Preserve all four routes, one checkpoint/category, seeds 0/42, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, diagnostic interfaces, and matching predictor serialization. Specify deterministic tokenization and cache invalidation as below.

Prioritize the baseline comparison, then capacity and frequency-bucket text-permutation controls within budget. Word-order shuffling cannot test mean pooling. Track ranks and tenth-negative thresholds because logit scaling can inflate margins without changing HR. Select only pinned macro HR@10; paired intervals exclude adaptive-selection bias and sampled metrics do not establish full-catalog gains [8,9]. No experiments were executed.

idea.description: Add a lightweight title/description encoder trained from scratch to the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Jointly learn a gated residual text contribution to each item-ID representation, using the identical fused representation for observed-history inputs and candidate scoring. Train one network and deploy one selected checkpoint per category. Retain this representation intervention as the first experiment; keep BPR-max and temporal-memory alternatives as separate trials rather than combining changes before attribution.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broadly related products without a concrete purpose connection and media without identifiable connections to preferred artists, stories or sounds. Available titles and descriptions may provide more specific item evidence than IDs alone, potentially sharing lexical information across sparse items. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate and 0.0265 lower-tail margin motivate testing improved discrimination. These observations do not establish that text will help: lexical overlap can reproduce broad-category matching, and text cannot reliably establish equipment compatibility, ownership redundancy, quantities, current intent or mood. The selected idea explicitly targets the first two user failures and weak model separation, with effectiveness requiring measured validation and qualitative evidence.
idea.implementation_notes:
Implement against the supplied corrected baseline; its source and resolved configuration were not included in the report. Preserve its GRU architecture, dimensions, optimizer, objective, sampling, clipping, dropout and checkpoint-selection schedule for the first comparison. Record the actual resolved values rather than inventing baseline settings. Resolve the host epoch setting, including SASREC_EPOCHS, within the 200-epoch maximum, retaining 200 batches per epoch. If the baseline already uses BPR-max, the objective alternative is not a distinct intervention until a concrete comparator is specified.

Use only host-provided public item titles/descriptions, interaction histories and permitted timestamps. Do not use review text or ratings, item ratings/categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, hidden interactions or external weights. Earlier generic metadata examples do not authorize those unavailable fields. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, supplied splits, all four category routes and the pinned evaluator. Write all generated artifacts under the trial directory. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

To make the new text component reproducible, use the following explicit initial configuration, recorded as proposal settings rather than baseline facts: normalize strings with Unicode NFKC and casefold; tokenize with Python's Unicode regular expression r'\w+'; concatenate up to 16 title tokens followed by up to 48 description tokens. Use no stemming, stop-word filtering or word-order features. Construct a category-specific vocabulary from text belonging to items observed in training histories, capped at 30,000 tokens including PAD=0 and UNK=1. Sort by decreasing token frequency with lexicographic tie breaking. Encode other host-provided catalog text using that frozen vocabulary; never use held-out interactions to build it. Missing text has an all-zero mask. Save the tokenizer specification, vocabulary, item-to-token table, masks and item-ID mapping. Inspect only permitted metadata values through the host's supplied mapping; never reconstruct alignment from assumptions about ID order.

Use token dimension equal to the baseline item embedding dimension. Initialize token embeddings from a zero-mean normal distribution with standard deviation 0.02 and keep PAD zero. Pool using masked sum divided by the nonpadding count clamped to one. Use a bias-free linear projection into the baseline item embedding dimension, initialized with Xavier uniform weights. Define e_i = v_i + has_text_i * sigmoid(w^T[v_i;t_i]+b) * P(t_i), where t_i is pooled text. Initialize gate weights to zero and b = log(0.1/0.9), approximately -2.197. Explicitly zero missing-text contributions and complete padding representations. The 0.1 gate is a conservative hypothesis, not exact baseline equivalence; text and ID norms may differ and must be measured. Optimize all new parameters jointly with the baseline optimizer and its existing parameter-group policy, documenting how new weights and biases are assigned. Retain baseline loss and do not add alignment losses or semantic mining initially.

Encode only unique IDs needed across histories, positive targets and sampled negatives in each training forward pass, reconstructing positions through differentiable indexing using torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True). Do not detach the text branch or reuse detached evaluation vectors during training. PyTorch unique may sort internally even with sorted=False; treat efficiency as something to profile, not a guaranteed improvement. EmbeddingBag is an optional equivalent masked-mean implementation only after checking empty bags and padding behavior. Preserve baseline transforms and scoring, replacing every relevant item lookup consistently; do not silently replace an untied output head with tied dot-product scoring. The report's dot-product pseudocode assumes that this matches the supplied scoring contract. If the baseline has distinct input/output ID tables, preserve them and apply the same jointly learned text encoder through explicitly documented head-compatible projections, keeping all parameters inside the one model.

Preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, and all host ModelView interfaces. A composite item module does not automatically satisfy nn.Embedding.weight semantics: provide effective-embedding lookup and bounded diagnostic sampling deliberately. If the actual adapter directly indexes item_emb.weight, adapt that adapter/probe to effective representations while preserving its external contract; exposing only ID weights would omit the intervention. Do not rebuild a full differentiable catalog every time .weight is accessed. Preserve any required attributes using the actual host implementation as the reference.

Keep causal next-item inputs unchanged and never expose the shifted target. Preserve the corrected GRU's padding policy: padding must not update recurrent states. Read the maximum index where sequence != 0, never count-1, and preserve explicit empty-history behavior. Do not reimplement fused recurrence merely to add text if the baseline already handles padding correctly. Verify empty, short and heavily left-padded histories before full training.

Each category must load exactly one jointly trained model/checkpoint. No independent text model, popularity or transition score, checkpoint averaging, independent expert or score fusion is allowed. During evaluation, compute detached effective catalog representations in bounded chunks only after loading the selected checkpoint and entering evaluation mode. Invalidate caches after optimizer updates, checkpoint loading, device/dtype changes or returning to training. Cache derived vectors only; they are deterministic outputs of the same checkpoint. Storage is approximately catalog_size times embedding_dimension times bytes_per_element, with additional tables if the baseline has separate scoring heads. Stream full-catalog scoring in chunks for the simulator's unseen-item recommendations to twenty training users, five per category, without changing the host evaluator or allocating an unnecessary complete user-by-catalog matrix.

Update the embedded predictor writer with the same text configuration, serialized vocabulary/token tables, architecture, transforms, scoring and state-dict layout. Load artifacts relative to the trial/predictor location. Check that freshly loaded predictor scores match the selected in-memory model on identical histories and candidates in eval mode, including missing text and padding. Use float32 atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 initially; investigate failures instead of silently widening tolerances. Measure ranking agreement alongside score differences, accounting for ties. Run bounded throughput/memory checks before committing to training; all GPU training, profiling, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Keep execution single-GPU.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), incorporating measured metrics and definitions. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Compute valid-position margins and embedding statistics through effective representations and the actual scoring head. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces without fabricating unavailable fields. Category breakdowns requiring unavailable item categories must be marked unavailable. Mapped cosine similarities around 0.5 do not justify a collapse penalty.

Record text coverage, UNK fraction, token-length distribution, text/ID norm ratio, and gate distributions excluding padding; these describe mechanism and failure risk rather than establish semantic understanding. Where available from the host's fixed candidate scores, inspect positive rank, paired hit/miss transitions and positive score minus the tenth-highest negative score. Keep raw margin diagnostics, but explain their score-scale dependence: positive inference-only scaling changes margins while preserving ranks except numerical ties. Training-time temperature changes can alter learned rankings and would be separate interventions. Do not add candidate generation or change negatives to obtain these diagnostics.

Start with the corrected baseline versus fusion under unchanged selection and validation schedules. If budget permits, separately retrain a parameter-matched ID-only GRU control with a precisely specified active nonlinear residual item branch, matching added trainable parameters as closely as possible and reporting any mismatch. Then test a fixed item-to-text permutation within training-frequency buckets, retaining original item histories and labels. Define buckets by floor(log2(max(1, training_count))); permute complete text rows including masks within each bucket using a dedicated preprocessing RNG seeded 0, save the permutation and do not change the training RNG seed 42. Singleton buckets remain unchanged and their count is reported. These are alternative single-model trials, never combined at prediction. Random token-assignment controls preserving text lengths and token frequencies, and title-only versus description-only controls, are later options rather than a required early grid. Within-item word shuffling is uninformative for mean pooling because it is order-invariant.

If host-visible per-user validation outcomes are available, report HR@10 differences by target training frequency and by overlap between target tokens and observed-history tokens, with bin definitions fixed before inspecting results and small-bin counts disclosed. Zero overlap versus any overlap is a simple initial lexical split; frequency bins can reuse the stated log2 bins. These are descriptive analyses, never alternate selection metrics or permission to obtain hidden labels. Improvements beyond capacity and text-permutation controls, particularly on sparse targets and low-overlap examples, would support useful lexical sharing but would still not prove semantic understanding. Text may act as an item identifier, exploit popularity-correlated language, overemphasize common brands, or blur the specific distinctions the user wants. Inspect representative rejection reasons only where the simulator actually provides them.

Select using equal-weight four-category macro validation HR@10 only; log all attempted settings and per-category effects. With 200 users/category, one changed hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If the host exposes paired baseline/proposal hit indicators, use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with analysis-only RNG seed 42, resampling paired users within each category and recomputing the macro difference each time. Use the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of macro differences, not averaged category interval endpoints. If users overlap across categories, preserve user clusters. Omit the interval when paired outcomes are unavailable. The interval is conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates, excludes training-seed and candidate variability, and does not correct adaptive checkpoint or hyperparameter selection. Small selected gains remain provisional until the host's independent held-out evaluation. Sampled HR@10 against 99 negatives does not establish full-catalog retrieval quality or online utility; simulator feedback from twenty training users is qualitative. No experiments or performance improvements are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class TextItemRepresentation(nn.Module):
    # Preserve the actual baseline dimensions, transforms and scoring contract.
    def encode_unique(item_ids):
        unique_ids, inverse = torch.unique(item_ids.reshape(-1), return_inverse=True)
        ids = id_embedding(unique_ids)
        tokens = token_table[unique_ids]
        mask = token_mask[unique_ids]
        embedded = token_embedding(tokens)
        count = mask.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1)
        text = (embedded * mask[..., None]).sum(-2) / count
        alpha = sigmoid(gate(concat(ids, text)))
        residual = text_projection(text)
        residual = where(has_text[unique_ids, None], residual, zeros_like(residual))
        fused = ids + alpha * residual
        fused = where(unique_ids[:, None] != 0, fused, zeros_like(fused))
        return fused[inverse].reshape(*item_ids.shape, embedding_dim)

# Build/save deterministic training-text vocabulary and catalog token tables.
# Preserve PAD=0, UNK=1; NFKC/casefold; Unicode word tokens;
# title cap 16, description cap 48, vocabulary cap 30,000.
# All learned parameters are jointly optimized; there is no fitted text predictor.
for category in supplied_four_categories:
    seed_training(42)
    model = corrected_GRU4Rec_with_text_component(resolved_baseline_config)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            batch = unchanged_family_sample_batch()
            # Unique lookup may span history, positive and negative IDs.
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(model, batch)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
            invalidate_eval_cache()
        unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_text_configuration(category)

# Predictor reproduces effective input/output lookups and baseline scoring.
model.load_state_dict(selected_checkpoint)
model.eval()
invalidate_eval_cache()
features = model.log2feats(left_padded_history)
positions = arange(left_padded_history.shape[1])
last = where(left_padded_history != 0, positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
# Explicitly handle last == -1 using baseline empty-history behavior.
scores = baseline_empty_handling_or_score_final_feature(features, last, candidates)
write_matching_embedded_predictor()
verify_loaded_predictor_score_and_rank_parity()

# Optional eval cache is detached, built in bounded catalog chunks,
# and used only while checkpoint, mode, device and dtype remain fixed.
# Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader),
# metric_definitions and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis).
# Diagnose actual effective representations and actual model scores.

# Controls are independently retrained alternative trials, never inference fusion.
# Prioritize baseline comparison, then matched capacity, then saved bucketed
# text permutation; avoid an exhaustive early search grid.
if host_exposes_paired_validation_hits:
    rng = analysis_rng(seed=42)
    differences = fusion_hits - baseline_hits
    for replicate in range(10000):
        category_deltas = []
        for category in supplied_four_categories:
            indices = rng.choice(200, size=200, replace=True)
            category_deltas.append(mean(differences[category][indices]))
        macro_delta[replicate] = mean(category_deltas)
    interval = percentile(macro_delta, [2.5, 97.5])
    # Use cluster-preserving resampling if users overlap across categories.
    # This does not adjust for adaptive selection or training/candidate variation.

originality.positive: The precise scratch-trained residual text module, shared effective representations and constrained GRU4Rec integration define a concrete, attributable adaptation.
originality.negative: Feature-rich recurrent recommendation already combines IDs and lexical content, and text–ID fusion is established. No verified exact match does not establish novelty; the earlier score of 3 understated the closest prior art.

future_potential.positive: A controlled experiment can establish whether permitted lexical sharing improves specific matching across product and media domains, and identify when text helps sparse items.
future_potential.negative: Short or generic text can reinforce popularity and broad lexical shortcuts. Scratch-trained pooling lacks demonstrated semantic transfer, and sampled validation gains may not improve full-catalog user utility.

code_difficulty.positive: Masked pooling and a scalar gate preserve the GRU backbone and need no pretrained assets or additional interaction data.
code_difficulty.negative: The original score of 4 omitted effective item_emb compatibility, possible untied scoring heads, differentiable unique lookups, catalog-cache invalidation, metadata serialization and predictor parity. These integration requirements are material.

related_work.title: [1] CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes alignment between description embeddings and collaborative information, motivating recommendation-specific text representations.
limitations: Its LLM-derived embeddings and Transformer architecture do not satisfy this experiment’s constraints.
It does not establish gains for scratch-trained text fusion in GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: [2] ITS-Rec (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary describes encoding textual item information for recommendation.
limitations: Its BERT encoder and review inputs cannot be transferred to this task.
Only permitted titles and descriptions may inform the proposed adaptation.

related_work.title: [3] Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides established cross-entropy and BPR-max objectives for recurrent recommendation.
limitations: Objective recommendations do not demonstrate improvement on the pinned four-category benchmark.
BPR-max is a distinct proposed intervention only if it differs from the resolved baseline objective.

related_work.title: [4] Hard-BPR (2024)
contributions: Addresses false-negative effects in hard-negative learning for implicit recommendation.
limitations: Its setting does not establish efficacy for this sequential GRU4Rec task.

related_work.title: [5] LSARN (2023 preprint)
contributions: The supplied summary describes temporal GRU gates and mechanisms for short- and longer-term interests.
limitations: Its richer memory mechanisms require additional implementation and attribution experiments.
It provides conceptual motivation rather than benchmark evidence for the proposed alternatives.

related_work.title: [6] Hidasi et al. (2016), feature-rich recurrent session recommendation
contributions: Combines item IDs and additional features, including lexical text features, through recurrent recommendation architectures.
Provides closer GRU-family precedent than pretrained Transformer-based text recommenders.
limitations: The supplied summary describes sparse unigram/bigram features rather than the exact proposed pooled-token residual.
It does not establish improvement under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: [7] TedRec
contributions: Studies text–ID fusion and motivates accounting for differences between the two representation sources.
limitations: Its findings caution against assuming simple addition is sufficient.
The supplied evidence does not validate this proposal's gate, initialization or scratch-trained encoder.

related_work.title: [8] Krichene and Rendle, On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model-comparison reversals.
limitations: This motivates careful interpretation rather than changing the mandated evaluator.
Fixed candidates improve comparability but do not remove sampling bias.

related_work.title: [9] Cawley and Talbot, On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation estimates.
limitations: It does not quantify the selection bias of these particular trials.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive winner selection.

related_work.title: [10] PyTorch torch.unique documentation
contributions: Documents unique-ID extraction and inverse indices useful for reconstructing repeated item lookups.
limitations: Internal sorting can limit performance benefits.
Documentation provides implementation semantics, not measured training speedups.

related_work.title: [11] PyTorch Embedding and EmbeddingBag documentation
contributions: EmbeddingBag supports pooled token embeddings without materializing all token vectors.
The related Embedding interface documents a learnable weight matrix: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Embedding.
limitations: A composite text–ID representation needs deliberate compatibility with consumers expecting item_emb.weight.
Empty inputs, padding and projection biases require explicit handling.

related_work.title: [12] SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling; the proposal applies the principle within categories and recomputes macro differences.
limitations: Requires paired observed outcomes.
User bootstrap uncertainty excludes training-seed variability, fixed-candidate uncertainty and adaptive selection bias.

related_work.title: [13] TASTE
contributions: The supplied search summary reports accuracy improvements and reduced popularity bias with a substantially different text-based recommendation approach.
limitations: Its language-model results do not establish comparable benefits for randomly initialized mean-pooled tokens.
They do not by themselves distinguish semantic transfer from lexical identification or popularity correlations.

related_work.title: [14] Recformer
contributions: The supplied search summary reports low-resource and cold-start benefits from language-based recommendation.
limitations: Its architecture and pretrained language representations do not transfer directly to this constrained GRU experiment.
Its results do not prove semantic understanding or gains from the proposed scratch-trained encoder.
